sections.heading: Roof Repair or Roof Replacement? The 25% Rule and 20-Year-Old Shingles

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: Roofers use it as a rule of thumb: once damage covers more than about 25% of a roof, replacement is usually more cost-effective than patching. New Jersey's code draws a line at the same number, since repairing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months on a commercial, multi-family, or attached building requires a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.

Not automatically. A 20-year-old 3-tab asphalt covering is at the end of its typical service life, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, while architectural asphalt runs about 30 years and slate far longer, so age alone does not decide it. Widespread granule loss, curling, soft decking, or leaks that move after each patch point to replacement; isolated damage calls for a targeted fix.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit from Montclair for a roof repair?

runs.v: Work on the covering of a detached one- or two-family home, even a full replacement, is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no construction permit, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code. On a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, work on more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months requires a permit, so confirm with the Montclair construction office before work on a storefront or multi-family building.

faqs.q: Does a roof repair on a Montclair historic-district home need a Certificate of Appropriateness?

runs.v: It can. Appearance-changing work on a property in a historic district or on a local landmark can need extra review, while a like-for-like repair usually changes nothing visible, so confirm the parcel's status with the Montclair construction office before work. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private owner.

faqs.q: Why does my Montclair Tudor keep leaking at the wall-to-roof junction?

runs.v: A recurring leak at a Tudor's wall-to-roof transition usually traces to deteriorated step flashing where the stucco, timber, or siding wall meets the shingles, and the water then follows the framing into the wall cavity and shows up below the actual entry point. Our team reseals the metal at the transition rather than caulking the surface symptom.

faqs.q: How do you repair slate and copper detailing on a Montclair Victorian?

runs.v: Broken slate is swapped tile by tile and corroded fasteners and copper valley metal are rebuilt in kind while the deck and nailers stay sound, with replacement material matched in design, color, and texture to every detail, the in-kind principle of Standard 6 of the Secretary of the Interior's Standards.
